name: Banaspati
description: A Javanese (and broader Indonesian) supernatural being most commonly described as a hovering ball of phosphorescent flame appearing near graveyards, old trees, and lonely roads at night. The name derives from the Sanskrit Vanaspati, 'Lord of the Forest'.

aliases.name: Vanaspati
aliases.meaning: 'Lord of the forest', literally 'one whose lord is the forest' — Vedic term for a great tree

origin: Most strongly attested in Java, with cognate traditions in Bali, Madura, and parts of Sumatra. The architectural Banaspati Raja face is found on Hindu-Buddhist temples across Java, with related Kala-faces across Bali and the wider Southeast Asian Hindu-Buddhist culture sphere.
